overview: Land’s End is the westernmost tip of mainland England, where granite cliffs drop straight into the Atlantic. The headland is part of a 110-acre stretch of protected coastline, and on a clear day you can pick out Wolf Rock lighthouse out to sea.

Behind the cliffs is a privately run visitor site with a hotel, cafés, shops and a cluster of paid family attractions, plus the famous signpost where people queue for a photo. You can ignore all of that and simply walk the coast path in either direction: the paths are open all year, whatever is happening at the visitor centre.

expect.title: Cliff-top walking
expect.text: Signed paths run along the clifftops, and the coast path carries on north towards Sennen. The rocks here formed around 270 million years ago, which is why the coastline looks so jagged.

expect.title: Birds and sea life
expect.text: Seabirds such as gannets, fulmars, kittiwakes, shags and razorbills are regulars, and the rare Cornish chough is sometimes seen. Bring binoculars.

expect.title: Family attractions
expect.text: A combined ticket covers four attractions: an indoor 15-hole adventure golf course, a walk-through Aardman exhibit, a short 4D film and a small farm with animals. They close over winter and reopen in spring.

expect.title: The signpost
expect.text: The famous Land’s End signpost is run as a paid photo experience, so expect a queue in summer.

goodToKnow.label: Parking
goodToKnow.text: Parking is paid; the money goes towards looking after the protected landscape. Check the website before you go for current arrangements and the locals’ discount.

goodToKnow.label: Opening
goodToKnow.text: The coast paths are open all year. The family attractions, cafés and shops keep shorter hours and close for maintenance in winter, and everything on site can be affected by bad weather.

goodToKnow.label: Food
goodToKnow.text: There’s a café looking out over the farm and the sea, a takeaway kiosk with pasties and ice cream, picnic benches, and a hotel restaurant and bar.

goodToKnow.label: Time to allow
goodToKnow.text: An hour is enough for the headland and a short walk; allow longer if you plan to do the attractions or walk part of the coast path.

setting.note: Clifftop walks plus indoor family attractions
